question:
A full-wave bridge rectifier with a capacitor filter is fed by a transformer secondary of $9\,\text{V}_{rms}$ at $50\,\text{Hz}$. The filter capacitor is $C=1000\,\mu\text{F}$ and each conducting diode drop is $0.70\,\text{V}$; two diodes conduct. The load resistance is initially $R_L=1.0\,\text{k}\Omega$ and later changed to $R_L=200\,\Omega$.

Use the approximations:</br>

$V_m=V_{rms}\sqrt{2},\quad V_p\approx V_m-1.40,\quad f_r=2f,$</br>

$\Delta V_{pp}\approx \frac{I_L}{f_r C},\quad V_{dc}\approx V_p-\frac{\Delta V_{pp}}{2},\quad I_L\approx \frac{V_{dc}}{R_L}$.

(a) For $R_L=1.0\,\text{k}\Omega$, compute $V_{dc}$ and $\Delta V_{pp}$.</br>

(b) For $R_L=200\,\Omega$, compute $V_{dc}$ and $\Delta V_{pp}$.</br>

(c) A student claims: “Ripple voltage does not depend on load; it depends only on the capacitor.” Evaluate this claim using your results.</br>

(d) Design a new capacitor value $C_{new}$, keeping the same rectifier and transformer, so that at $R_L=200\,\Omega$, the ripple peak-to-peak remains equal to the ripple obtained in part (a). Show your reasoning.</br>

(e) Draw the circuit and sketch the capacitor-filtered output waveforms for both loads, clearly indicating how discharge between peaks changes.

Present the calculated results and conclusions.

options.A: At $R_L=1\,\text{k}\Omega$: $V_{dc}\approx 11.27\,\text{V}$ and $\Delta V_{pp}\approx 0.113\,\text{V}$; at $R_L=200\,\Omega$: $V_{dc}\approx 11.05\,\text{V}$ and $\Delta V_{pp}\approx 0.553\,\text{V}$; claim is incorrect because ripple increases with load current; to keep ripple same at $200\,\Omega$, need $C_{new}\approx 5000\,\mu\text{F}$ (about $5\times$).
options.B: At $R_L=1\,\text{k}\Omega$: $V_{dc}\approx 9.00\,\text{V}$ and $\Delta V_{pp}\approx 1.13\,\text{V}$; at $R_L=200\,\Omega$: $V_{dc}\approx 9.00\,\text{V}$ and $\Delta V_{pp}\approx 1.13\,\text{V}$; claim is correct; $C_{new}=1000\,\mu\text{F}$ is sufficient.
options.C: At $R_L=1\,\text{k}\Omega$: $V_{dc}\approx 11.27\,\text{V}$ and $\Delta V_{pp}\approx 0.113\,\text{V}$; at $R_L=200\,\Omega$: $V_{dc}\approx 12.7\,\text{V}$ and $\Delta V_{pp}\approx 0.113\,\text{V}$; claim is correct; $C_{new}$ must be smaller to reduce ripple.
options.D: Ripple depends only on frequency, not on $R_L$; changing $R_L$ changes only $V_{dc}$ but keeps $\Delta V_{pp}$ same; hence $C_{new}$ is not needed.
